data.long_meaning: From the Latin word 'lux', meaning 'light'. Derived from the Roman family name 'Lucanus'. In Christianity, St. Lucindus is a martyr and bishop venerated in the Eastern Orthodox Church. The name Lucindus carries the meaning “Light, bright, shining” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Lucindus usually hope their child will grow to embody light, bright, shining and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_latin.name: Lucindus
in_latin.meaning: Lucindus nomen Christianum ex Lucinde derivatum est, significans lucem et virtutem.
in_latin.long_meaning: Lucindus nomen Christianum est, quod ex Lucinde derivatum est, significans lucem et virtutem. In historia ecclesiae, nomen huius generis fuerunt multa, qui in Christo crediderunt et virtutes suas in Deo manifestaverunt. Lucindus nomen est testimonium Dei in mundo, qui in tenebris lucem afferit et virtutes in homines infundit.

He is said to have been a disciple of Saint Norreth of Xanten and lived at the Benedictine monastery in Cologne, Germany. His feast day is celebrated on November 28th.

Saint Lucindus of Beauvais is a legendary saint who is said to have lived in the 3rd century. According to legend, he was a Roman soldier who converted to Christianity and renounced the military. He is said to have been tortured and martyred for his faith in Beauvais, France. His feast day is celebrated on the 16th of March.
